const ONLY = [];   // smoke test: e.g. ['T9', 'T1']. Leave empty to run all.

const tests = [
  { test_id: 'T1',  input_text: 'The user should be able to filter reports by date range, category, and status. Results must load in under 2 seconds. PM: Sarah. Deadline: Q3.' },
  { test_id: 'T2',  input_text: 'We need better reporting. Something like what Competitor X has.' },
  { test_id: 'T3',  input_text: 'The dashboard should auto-refresh every 5 seconds. [Later in same meeting] Performance is critical, minimize API calls.' },
  { test_id: 'T4',  input_text: 'Users need to export reports as PDF and CSV. PDF must include company logo. CSV must preserve formulas.' },
  { test_id: 'T5',  input_text: 'Discussed dashboard... John mentioned something about real-time... budget TBD...' },
  { test_id: 'T6',  input_text: 'Engineering wants microservices. Design wants single-page app. PM wants it shipped by March.' },
  { test_id: 'T7',  input_text: 'API must support 10,000 concurrent users. Response time < 200ms at p95. Must integrate with Salesforce REST API v52.' },
  { test_id: 'T8',  input_text: 'Admins need bulk user management. End users need a simplified view. Auditors need read-only access with full history.' },
  { test_id: 'T9',  input_text: 'Meeting happened. Notes: none.' },
  { test_id: 'T10', input_text: 'SSO login requires the new auth service which is being built by Team Alpha. ETA unknown.' }
];

return tests
  .filter(t => !ONLY.length || ONLY.includes(t.test_id))
  .map(t => ({ json: { ...t, input_type: 'transcript' } }));
